Maria Chen: Hey all — I accepted the org invite but I can't see the `redwood/bootcamp` repo. I get a 404 when I go to the repo URL. Anyone know who I should ping? :wave:
Alex Rivera: Hi Maria — welcome! Did you accept the SSO prompt on GitHub? Sometimes that blocks repo access until you do.
Maria Chen: I think so? I clicked 'Authorize' when the invite popped up. How can I check?
Tanay Singh: You can confirm under Settings -> Applications -> Authorized OAuth Apps or try this: `https://github.com/orgs/redwood/sso?api=true` (open in browser) — if your session isn't linked it will show a message.
Maria Chen: Ran that link, it says: "You need to complete your SSO authorization to access this organization."
Sarah O'Neil: Okay that means SSO didn't fully bind. @Alex can you trigger a resend of the SSO link?
Alex Rivera: Sure, doing that now. Onboarding-bot will also post instructions.
onboard-bot: Hi Maria — I've sent an SSO re-auth link to your work email. Please click it and then try the org page again. If that doesn't work, reply here with `ssolog` and we'll look up the audit.
Maria Chen: Clicked the link and authorized. Still 404. Also trying to `git clone git@github.com:redwood/bootcamp.git` gives: "Permission denied (publickey)."
Jordan Patel: Two things: 1) Team membership — you should be on the `engineers` team with repo access. 2) SSH key — do you have an SSH key added to your GitHub account? Run `ssh -T git@github.com` to test.
Maria Chen: Running `ssh -T git@github.com` returns: "Hi mariach! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access." so SSH looks fine.
Tanay Singh: SSH is good. 404 + successful SSH auth often means the user isn't in the correct team/org role. Alex, can you check Maria's team membership in the org?
Alex Rivera: I see Maria as a member of org but not assigned to `engineers`. Assigning now... done. Maria, try the repo URL again.
Maria Chen: Repo visible now, thanks! Can still not push — permission denied on `git push`. Error: "remote: You don’t have permission to push to this repository."
Jordan Patel: That usually means you're not a write member for that repo. `engineers` team should be write; I'll confirm perms.
Jordan Patel: Confirmed — `engineers` has write on `bootcamp`. Maria, are you on the repo branch protection or trying to push to `main`? We protect main and require PRs.
Maria Chen: Ah, trying to push directly to `main`. Will open a PR. Thanks!
Sarah O'Neil: Quick note for the future: new-hire checklist has steps for SSO + team mapping + SSH. If anything else pops up ping #new-hires or me directly. :sparkles:
Maria Chen: Sweet — all set now. Thanks everyone! :heart:
